newsitem.title: FRANCE: Santer urges EU leaders not to wreck EU reforms.
newsitem.headline: Santer urges EU leaders not to wreck EU reforms.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer urged European Union states on Wednesday not to jeopardise plans to approve wide-ranging reforms to the EU at a summit in Amsterdam next week.

"If we can make improvements let's do that, but let's not jeopardise the project by last minute special pleading which may undermine the balance we have arrived at," Santer told the European Parliament.

He was speaking two days after France's new Socialist government threw the EU's plans for a single currency into confusion by asking for more time to study a previously agreed stability pact to keep budget deficits tight after the currency is launched on January 1, 1999.

The pact was supposed to be ratified by EU leaders in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17 at the same time as they approved internal EU reforms in a revised treaty designed to prepare the 15-member bloc for its ambitious expansion eastward.

The European Commission is rushing to find a way to meet France's concerns, which revolve around its view that job creation should play a more important role in the EU's plans for economic and monetary union (EMU).

Because employment is also an issue in the EU's negotiations on a new treaty, a number of officials have worried that the advent of the new government will also mean that the treaty cannot be completed in Amsterdam.

Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, whose country holds the EU presidency, told the EU assembly he was confident the French would find a solution to allow the stability pact to be approved at Amsterdam, "but it's not in the bag yet".

Santer said the Amsterdam summit should not backtrack on provisional agreements to give the EU more powers to act on issues which concerned its citizens, especially unemployment and social issues, free movement of people around the Union, health and consumer protection.

He urged EU governments to reach a deal next week which would reconcile efforts to create a Union more integrated with the needs of its citizens, to give the EU a strong united voice in world affairs backed up by military capacity and to make its own institutions more efficient and democratic in time for enlargement.
